- If sentiment is positive and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- When sentiment shows strong upward trend (e.g., >0.6 over 3–5 days), avoid over-forecasting; cap 30d forecast at 10–15% above recent 18d mean.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, reduce the spike by 10–20% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >10% in 3–5 consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until within 5% of recent 18d average.  
- For sentiment <0.2, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect weak market sentiment.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3 in 3 days), smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before applying trend adjustments.
